chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: Ali ibn al-Mughira narrated to me, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and offered him the choice, and indicated to him humility, and was his advisor. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat the food of a slave and sit the sitting of a slave, out of humility to Allah, the Exalted.

Then he came to him at the time of death with the keys of the treasures of the world, and said: These are the keys of the treasures of the world which your Lord has sent to you, so that there will be for you all that the earth carries, without anything being reduced from you.
So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the companions of the Most High'.

key_terms.الرَّفِيقُ الْأَعْلَى: The Companion of the Most High (a reference to Paradise/Prophets)
key_terms.مَفَاتِيحُ خَزَائِنِ الدُّنْيَا: Keys of the treasures of the world

ai.seo_question: What choice did the Prophet Muhammad receive from Jibraeel regarding worldly wealth versus humility?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s voluntary asceticism (zuhd) as a divine choice rather than mere necessity, illustrating the Shia emphasis on humility as a spiritual virtue. The narrative contrasts the transient nature of worldly power with the eternal reward of the Hereafter, reinforcing the concept that true nobility lies in closeness to God. This event is often cited by scholars to demonstrate the Prophet’s perfect adherence to the divine command to remain humble despite his status.

The Rasool<sup>saww</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup> used to eat like the eating of the slave, and sit like the sitting of the slave being humble to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> was given (by Jibraeel) at the time of his<sup>saww</sup> death, the Keys of the treasures of the world. The Rasool<sup>saww</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> (want to be) among the friends of the Most High<sup>azwj</sup>’.
